shortDescription: Austria's coalition government said on Monday it will extend its so-called petrol price brake, a measure aimed at cushioning the blow to consumers of higher oil prices from the conflict in the Middle East, by another month in its current pared-down form.($1 = 0.8624 euros)

children: Austria's coalition government said on Monday it will extend its so-called petrol price brake, a measure aimed at cushioning the blow to consumers of higher oil prices from the conflict in the Middle East, by another month in its current pared-down form.

The measure was introduced in April with two components: a cap on retailers' margins and a cut in petrol tax, which together totalled 10 euro cents (12 cents) per litre. The margin cap was scrapped in June.
The conservative-led government will extend the current 1.9 cent per litre petrol tax cut by another month until the end of September, the economy ministry said in a statement.
Each extension lasts a month and at the end of the month the three ruling centrist parties discuss whether and in what form to renew it.
Critics including the far-right Freedom Party say the measure is too small to make any meaningful difference to consumers.

"The petrol price brake remains an important government instrument in the fight against inflation," junior minister Michaela Schmidt of the Social Democrats, who represents her party in government negotiations, was quoted as saying in the statement.
